headline: Wall Street is starting to question whether Anthropic can justify a 2 trillion dollar price when it lists next month.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: follow-up on the week's biggest IPO story, but the Times' own arguments could not be read.
importance_line: The first big AI-lab float sets the price for the whole sector and for the savers who will be offered shares, and the new element is doubt about the valuation rather than the timetable.
summary: The Times reports that Anthropic, a lossmaking company seeking a listing larger than SpaceX's while its own filing warns of the harm its AI systems could cause, faces a Wall Street reality check over its planned 2 trillion dollar valuation; this follows Bloomberg's report of 1 Oct 2026 that the company targets a float before Thanksgiving. Reuters' review of the prospectus, as relayed by The Sydney Morning Herald and The Observer, shows a 2025 operating loss of about 8 billion dollars within a 42 billion dollar net loss, 47 percent of sales routed through Amazon and Google, and a Broadcom loan of up to 42 billion dollars that the filing itself flags as a possible conflict of interest.
notes: Desk-built entry: Times headline and standfirst only (paywall); facts from Reuters and Bloomberg as carried in SMH (C07-06) and The Observer (C07-05) read today. Follow-up of 1002:C06-01.
